text: 5-year-old boy. The patient is presented by his mother for a well-child visit. speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you. Since this was found incidentally, I need to rule out secondary causes. Can you tell me if he has any symptoms of urinary tract infections, or if his urine appears foamy or bloody? Also, has he had any episodes of severe headaches or visual disturbances?

text: My main symptom is High blood pressure on the right upper extremity.

speaker: Doctor
text: It is crucial to check if this blood pressure elevation is isolated to one arm, which could suggest a vascular issue like coarctation of the aorta or subclavian artery stenosis. speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant past medical history. Born full term with an uneventful neonatal period. Social history: Patient attends kindergarten. Lives with parents and one younger sibling. No exposure to tobacco smoke.

speaker: Doctor
text: I will now proceed with a directed cardiovascular examination to check for radio-femoral delay and auscultate for any murmurs or bruits. I also need to assess his lower extremity pulses and blood pressure to compare with the upper extremity readings.
